title: Showing off

cards: Who was watching the last time you did something good? A door held, a donation, a long prayer, a kind comment under someone's post. Sometimes nobody saw.
Sometimes the whole room did. The deed looks the same either way. A short surah of the Qur'an, al-Ma'un, turns on exactly this.
It speaks of worshippers who pray, and still says woe to them, because of why they pray. Today, the disease that can live inside a good deed: showing off, what Arabic calls riya'.

teach.b: First, a callback to ikhlas, four days ago: actions are by intentions, the hadith that opens Sahih al-Bukhari. Riya' is the same good deed, aimed at the wrong eyes. Second, the surah.
Pickthall's words: "Ah, woe unto worshippers Who are heedless of their prayer; Who would be seen (at worship)". Then the twist: they would be seen, and yet they refuse small kindnesses.
The prayer done for an audience sits right next to a hand that won't pass the salt. Showing off and stinginess keep company. Third, a picture from al-Baqarah.
Charity given to be seen by people is like a smooth rock with a little soil on it. Heavy rain comes, and the rock is left bare. Nothing could take root.
Fourth, the cure, which is not hiding everything. The Qur'an praises those who give by night and by day, in secret and openly; public good can teach and invite.
But a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari describes a person Allah shades on a day with no other shade: someone who gives charity so quietly that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand gave.
So the practice isn't never be seen. It's keeping a few good deeds where only Allah sees them, so the heart remembers who they were for.

how: Muslim teachers warn against riya', doing good to be seen, starting from the hadith that actions are by intentions; some keep part of their charity and extra prayer private, while public giving is also praised in the Qur'an.

o: doing good in order to be seen by people
boasting about money, looks or success
letting others see a good deed at all

s: the Qur'an says all good deeds must be hidden
it praises those who give by night and day, in secret and openly.
al-Ma'un links praying to be seen with refusing small kindnesses
they would be seen at worship, and yet refuse small kindnesses.
in al-Baqarah, charity for show is like soil on a rock the rain washes bare

games.q: you've given to a good cause. a friend asks what you've been up to this week. what does today's teaching lean toward?
o: post a screenshot of the receipt.
keep this one between you and Allah.
never give again, in case it's riya'.
games.why: the hadith praises giving so quietly the left hand doesn't know. giving openly isn't forbidden, but a few hidden deeds keep the intention clear.

practice: Choose one good thing you could do that nobody will find out about: paying for something anonymously, fixing what someone else broke and saying nothing, praying a little longer when no one is near.
See it done, notice the small itch to mention it later, and let the itch be. If you pray, you can ask that it be accepted; if you don't, let the deed be enough without a witness.

wordCard.voice: Showing off. Riya': doing good in order to be seen; in the Qur'an, soil on a smooth rock that the rain washes away. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: showing off, doing good to be seen by people.

carryVoice: Your line: not for eyes. The left hand doesn't need to know. Tomorrow, a disease that burns hot and fast: anger.
